name: test-tier-boundaries
body: Every test in the repo belongs to exactly one of three tiers, defined by its body, and the layout must expose them to separate selection. **unit** — exactly one unit under test, everything else faked; pure in-memory (no filesystem, database, git or process). **int** — two or more units wired together; still pure in-memory (filesystem/database/git/process faked). **e2e** — one or more units with real I/O of any kind: any filesystem access (including `std::env::temp_dir()`/`TempDir`), opening `db.lbug`, any git operation, or any process spawn. The body wins over any name or evidence list. **Layout:** unit and int tests live in a sibling `tests.rs` of their source module, preserving the module path so libtest's `…::tests::unit::` and `…::tests::int::` filters select them; every e2e test lives in a top-level `tests/` integration crate (one per source module, sharing a `tests/common/mod.rs` helper module) and carries `#[ignore = "e2e tier: …; run via cargo test-e2e"]`, so a plain `cargo test` — the default unit+int gate — can never reach it. Non-test helpers stay at the test-module root (or in the shared `common` module), never inside a tier submodule. A tier may select zero tests.
